sentences.text:
This appeal is preferred under Section 374 (2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 against the judgment dated 16.10.2003 passed by Learned 9th Additional Sessions Judge (FTC) in S.T. No.
161/2003, wherein the said Court convicted the appellant and sentenced him as under:-
Conviction Sentence U/S 354 of Indian Penal R.I. for one year.
Code U/S 323 of Indian Penal R.I. for Six months.

Code (Both sentences shall run concurrently)
2.

As per case of the prosecution, on 28.04.2003, at about 10.00 PM, complainant/victim (PW-02)
lodged an FIR against the appellant at police Station- Gariyaband i.e. Ex.P/4 and stated in FIR that on the date of incident i.e. 28.04.2003 at evening she went to her friend's house namely Pushpa for answering the nature call, but, she found that her Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19792 friend was not Charan Singh vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 15 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84907689/
1 present, only her mother was present and when she returned from her friend's house, at that time accused/appellant kept her hand and pulled her in the house of Somti Bai and put her down her in Somti Bai's house.

sentences.text: When, she shouted for help, then Somti Bai came to the rescue of the complainant/victim, but appellant pushed and shooed her away.

Thereafter, the appellant/accused after removing clothes of the complainant/ victim, appellant tried to commit sexual intercourse with her due to which she again shouted for help, the accused/appellant closed her mouth and brushed her breast and when she was trying to free herself from the appellant at that time her uncle Preetram (PW-04) and grandfather Jagatram (PW- 03) reached the spot and ran for rescuing the complainant/victim (PW-02) from the appellant, but the accused/appellant assaulted her uncle Preetram (PW-04) and also her grandfather Jagatram (PW- 03) and due to assaulted by appellant,
her uncle and grandfather received injuries on their bodies and the complainant/victim (PW-02)
stated that if at the time of incident, her uncle and grandfather did not come to rescue her, then the accused would have committed rape with her.

Thereafter the matter was registered in the police Station for offence Under Section 376 and 323 of IPC as Crime No. 28/2003.
3.
During investigation the accused/appellant was arrested and medical examination was conducted of both the parties.

The charge-sheeted filed before the learned Judicial Magistrate, Gariyaband,
thereafter the matter was committed to the 9th Additional Sessions Judge (FTC), Raipur and the appellant was put for trial for offence punishable under Sections 376 read with Section 511 and 323 of IPC against the appellant.
Conclusion Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19792 of the trial is that the appellant has been convicted as mentioned in Para 1 of this judgment.
4. So as to hold the accused/appellant guilty, the prosecution has examined as many as 08 witnesses.
Statement of the accused/appellant was also recorded under Section 313 of Cr.P.C. in which he denied the charges leveled against him and pleaded innocence and false implication in the case.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the learned trial Court has not properly evaluated the material available on record and wrongly reached to a conclusion and convicted the appellant and as such the impugned judgement deserves to be set aside, the prosecution has failed to establish ingredients of outrage of modesty beyond reasonable doubt.
He further submits that complainant/victim (PW-02) in her statement admitted the fact that they were in love and it is clear that she used to meet the appellant at various places.

PW-03 and PW-04 have not supported the prosecution story and further stated that PW-03 & PW- 04 reached the spot of incident at the time of commission of offence, but they have not stated that the appellant tried to have sexual intercourse with the complainant/victim (PW-02).
He further submits that the learned trial Court did not appreciate oral and documentary evidence.
Prosecution has utterly failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt, so impugned judgment is liable to be set aside.
He further submits that this incident took place in the year 2003 and the appellant is now 45 years middle- aged person and during course of trial he remained in jail for more than 03 months.

He further submits that if conviction of Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19792 appellant is maintained, then he prays that his sentence may be liable to be reduced to the period already undergone by him and he remained in jail for more than 03 months and the incident took place in the year 2003.

sentences.text: 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State supported the impugned judgment and submits that the learned trial Court properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence and rightly convicted the appellant.

7. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material available on record including the impugned judgment.
8.
It is clear from record of learned Trial Court that the learned trial Court framed charges under Sections 376 read with Section 511 and 323 of IPC against the appellant.

Dr. B. Barah (PW-01)
opined that she did not find any external injury on the body of complainant/victim (PW-02)
and gave her report as Ex.P/1.
Complainant/victim (PW-02), Jagatram (PW- 03), Preetram (PW-04) & Smt. Somti Bai (PW-06) have categorically stated against the appellant.

Jagatram (PW-03) stated that when he tried to rescue his grandaughter from the appellant, then the appellant punched on his face due to which he received injuries and Dr. Smt. B. Barah (PW-01) who examined the injured person, Preetram (PW-04) and found injury on his face and gave her report as Ex.P/2.

Learned trial Court categorically appreciated oral and documentary evidence and acquitted the appellant for offence under Section 376 read with Section 511 of IPC, but the learned trial Court convicted the appellant for offence under Section 354 & 323 of IPC.
So, this Court finds that the learned trial Court rightly convicted the appellant under these sections.
Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:19792 9.
As regards sentence, keeping in view the facts that incident is said to have taken place in the year 2003 and thereby nearly 21 years said to have rolled by since then.
The appellant has already remained in jail for more than 03 months, therefore, his sentence is liable to be reduced to the period already undergone by him.
10. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court is of the opinion that the ends of justice would be met if the appellant is sentenced to the already undergone by him.
Accordingly, his sentence is reduced to the period already undergone by him.
However, the fine amount imposed by the Trial Court shall remain intact.
11. With these modifications, the appeal is partly allowed.

12. The appellant is reported to be on bail, therefore, his bail bond shall remain in operation for a period of six months from today in view of provision of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C.
13.
The trial Court record along with a copy of this judgment be sent back immediately to the trial Court concerned for compliance and necessary action.
